subject: Literature
title: Marilynne Robinson's Gilead
description: A 60-second lesson on Marilynne Robinson's Gilead.

hook.text: Marilynne Robinson waited twenty-four years between her first and second novels, and both won major literary prizes.

buildup.text: Gilead is a letter from a dying pastor to his young son, meditating on faith, regret, and the meaning of ordinary life.

discovery.text: Robinson writes about religion with an intellectual depth that makes secular readers take theology seriously as literature.

twist.text: In an era that rewards speed and productivity, Robinson publishes rarely and slowly, insisting that silence is part of writing.

climax.text: Robinson proved that quiet, contemplative fiction about faith can compete with the loudest novels of any generation.

punchline.text: She proved that silence between novels is not absence but depth.

quiz.question: What makes Robinson's approach to publishing unusual?
options: She publishes a new novel every year without fail
She publishes rarely and slowly, insisting that silence is part of writing
She writes under multiple pen names simultaneously
